name: UAE citizenship by nomination for investors and talents (amended Executive Regulation of Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 on Nationality and Passports)
notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme with a price: candidates (investors who own UAE property, doctors, scientists, inventors, artists, and their families) cannot apply; they are nominated by Rulers' and Crown Princes' courts, executive councils or the Cabinet. Dual nationality allowed; citizenship can be withdrawn if conditions are breached. No numbers of grants have been published. Announced by WAM on 30 Jan 2021; the amended regulation itself was not found.

name: UAE Golden Visa (الإقامة الذهبية - golden residence; long-term residence for investors, entrepreneurs and talents)
notes: Long-term residence without a sponsor. Created by Cabinet Resolution 56/2018 (in force 3 Feb 2019; permits issued from 21 May 2019): investors AED 10 million (10 years) or AED 5 million in property (5 years). Replaced by Cabinet Resolution 8/2021 (text not found), then by the annex to Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 (in force 3 Oct 2022): 10-year permits, AED 2 million in property, bank deposit or company share, or AED 250,000 a year in taxes. Issued by ICP federally and by GDRFA in Dubai. Gives no path to citizenship: there is no residence period that leads to naturalisation; citizenship is only by nomination (see are-citizenship-nomination). Official counts are press figures covering all golden-visa categories, mostly Dubai only; no investor-only series is published.

name: Argentina citizenship by investment (Ley de Ciudadanía 346, art. 2 inc. 2, as amended by Decreto 366/2025)
notes: Legal basis exists but no operating programme was found. Decree of necessity and urgency 366/2025 (28 May 2025) lets foreigners who make a "relevant investment" naturalise regardless of residence and creates the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión under the Ministry of Economy; Decreto 524/2025 sets the procedure; Ley 27802 (2026) settles tax residence of such citizens; the Agency got an executive director from 22 Apr 2026. The Ministry of Economy has to define what counts as a relevant investment: no such resolution was found in the Boletín Oficial up to 1 Oct 2026, so there are no published amounts. Whether Congress has reviewed or rejected the DNU was not checked.

name: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP)
notes: Set up by the Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 (gazetted 11 Apr 2013); run by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU). Routes: National Development Fund donation, real estate, business investment, and (from 2018) University of the West Indies Fund. 5,203 applications from inception to 30 Jun 2024.

name: Business Innovation and Investment Program (BIIP): Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa subclass 188, (Permanent) subclass 888, Business Talent subclass 132
notes: Umbrella programme for business and investor migrants under the Migration Regulations 1994. Provisional (subclass 188, four years; five years from July 2021) then permanent residence (888) if conditions are met; Australian citizenship can follow after the usual residence requirement for permanent residents. Streams over time: Business Innovation, Investor (AUD1.5m bonds 2012-2021; AUD2.5m complying investment 2021-2024), Significant Investor (see aus-siv), Premium Investor (2015-2021, AUD15m, not researched here), Entrepreneur, Business Talent, Venture Capital Entrepreneur. Most applicants needed state/territory nomination. Closed to new applications in July 2024 (1 July per the 2024-25 Migration Program report, 31 July per the visa website); on-hand applications still processed. Programme numbers are Migration Program places, primary and secondary applicants together.

name: Significant Investor visa (SIV): Significant Investor stream of the Business Innovation and Investment visa (subclass 188C provisional, 888C permanent)
notes: A stream within aus-biip, kept as its own programme because it is the "golden visa" part. AUD5 million complying investment held for the provisional visa (four years; five from July 2021), with Complying Investment Framework rules from 1 July 2015 and revised ratios from 1 July 2021. No points test; nomination by a state/territory government or Austrade. For permanent residence (888) the investor had to spend 40 days a year in Australia, or the spouse 180 days. Permanent residents can later apply for citizenship under the normal residence rules. 2,264 primary SIVs were granted to 31 Oct 2019; most applicants were Chinese nationals. Closed to new applications 31 July 2024.

name: Austrian citizenship in the special interest of the Republic (Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz 1985, § 10 Abs. 6, 'außerordentliche Leistungen')
notes: Not an advertised investment programme and no published price. A constitutional provision lets a Land grant citizenship without 10 years' residence, proof of income or renunciation of the old nationality when the federal government confirms that the person's past and expected 'extraordinary achievements' are in the special interest of the Republic. Used for scientists, artists, athletes and business people alike; official statistics do not split by field. Procedure regulated by BGBl. II 39/2014. Names and professions of confirmed persons are published (at least since 2016-2017). Statistik Austria counts 10 to 54 naturalisations a year in 2007-2023. The European Commission (COM(2019) 12, p. 4, fn. 10) lists Austria among states whose law equates national interest with economic interest. The 1965 start date comes from a ministry statement (8483/AB).

name: Bulgarian citizenship by investment (Закон за българското гражданство, art. 12a ordinary route and art. 14a fast-track route)
notes: Naturalisation for holders of investor permanent residence. Art. 12a (ordinary): after 5 years of permanent residence, investment of about EUR 500,000 (BGN 1 million). Art. 14a (fast track, added Feb 2013): after 1 year, investment increased to about EUR 1 million (BGN 2 million) or a priority-project route; no language test or real residence needed. Both repealed by the law in State Gazette no. 26 of 1 Apr 2022; pending procedures were ended and SANS was told to review past naturalisations. Ministry of Justice: 50 investor citizenships 2013-Jan 2019 (4 art. 12a, 46 art. 14a). launched=2005 is the year the Commission gives for the scheme's introduction; the fast track dates from 2013.

name: Bulgaria permanent residence for investors (Закон за чужденците в Република България, art. 25(1) items 6-8)
notes: Permanent (not temporary) residence permit for foreigners who invest, e.g. BGN 1 million in concession rights, collective investment schemes or alternative investment funds, BGN 2 million in listed shares or in a certified priority project, or BGN 6 million in an unlisted company (amounts as in the consolidated law on 2 Oct 2026). It was the first step to citizenship under arts. 12a/14a until 2022 and still exists. Ordinary naturalisation after 5 years of permanent residence remains possible under the general rules (language test etc.). Launch year not established; investor items date from 2005/2009 amendments. The Bulgarian Investment Agency certifies the investments: 981 persons certified 2014-Aug 2021 (both stages).

name: Belize economic citizenship programme
notes: Citizenship sold to 'economic citizens' under the Belize Nationality Act; the Act still mentions dependants of an 'economic citizen'. The US State Department listed Belize as selling economic citizenship in 2000 and 2001, at $25,000 per person (currency not stated), and reported that Belize announced it would stop in January 2002 after two buyers linked to a terrorist group were refused US visas. Start date, legal text and numbers sold not found.

name: Comoros economic citizenship programme (citoyenneté économique)
notes: Law on economic citizenship signed by President Sambi on 27 Nov 2008 after an earlier rejection (July 2008); a parliamentary inquiry later found the vote broke procedure. Mainly bulk sales to the UAE (and talks with Kuwait) to document stateless Bidoon, who did not move to Comoros; an initial deal of $200m for 4,000 families, then (2011) EUR 4,600 per passport with a minimum of 5,000. The IMF describes it as citizenship for KMF 1 million (about US$3,000) per person, with receipts routed via the Banque de France. Proceeds were large relative to GDP (IMF: about 3-4.5% in 2012 in 2013 reports, over 6% in the 2015 report). Passports were also sold outside the official channel, including to Iranians. Suspended after President Azali took office in May 2016. A parliamentary commission (set up June 2017, report Dec 2017) estimated missing revenue of $100m (Reuters) or $971m (AFP); the State Security Court sentenced ex-president Sambi to life for 'high treason' on 28 Nov 2022. Official law text and commission report not obtained.

name: Cyprus Investment Programme (Κυπριακό Επενδυτικό Πρόγραμμα, ΚΕΠ), incl. the 2007-2013 scheme for exceptional naturalisation of foreign investors
notes: Naturalisation by Council of Ministers decision, without residence: 2007-2013 under para 2(στ) of the Third Schedule of the Civil Registry Law (exceptional services), from 30 Apr 2013 under art. 111A(2) (Law 36(I)/2013), from 18 Aug 2020 under regulations ΚΔΠ 379/2020. Criteria changed 12 times by Council decisions. Abolished by decision of 13 Oct 2020: no applications after 31 Oct 2020; pending ones approved until 31 Jul 2021. 6,779 naturalisations to 17 Aug 2020 (inquiry); 3,517 investors and 3,810 family members to 31 Jul 2021 (Audit Office). Art. 111A(2) deleted by a law passed in late 2025 or early 2026; EU infringement closed 11 Mar 2026.

name: Cyprus fast-track permanent residence for investors (Άδεια Μετανάστευσης, Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations; 'golden visa')
notes: Permanent residence (Immigration Permit) for third-country investors, issued by the Minister of Interior under Regulation 6(2); EUR 300,000 investment plus EUR 50,000 annual income (2023 criteria). No right to work except as director of the invested company. Card valid 10 years; right of residence unlimited. It does not lead to citizenship by itself; naturalisation needs years of actual residence under the ordinary rules (not researched here). Launch date and pre-2021 terms not verified. No official numbers of permits found.

name: Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment Programme
notes: Originally the Economic Citizenship Programme (ECP); administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CBIU). Routes: Economic Diversification Fund contribution and approved real estate. Under EU request (June 2026) to phase out by 1 June 2028.

name: Egyptian citizenship through investment programmes (الجنسية المصرية بالبرامج الاستثمارية; Nationality Law 26/1975 Art. 4 bis)
notes: Naturalisation by Prime Minister's decree on the recommendation of a Cabinet unit (members from Foreign Affairs, Interior, Investment/International Cooperation and security agencies), under Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law as replaced by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019). Routes and amounts set by PM Decree 3099/2019 (Dec 2019; text not obtained), amended by PM Decrees 876/2023 (in force 3 Mar 2023) and 3562/2023 (19 Sep 2023); the unit was organised by PM Decree 647/2020. Current routes: property USD 300,000; investment project USD 350,000 plus USD 100,000 to the Treasury; USD 500,000 deposit at the Central Bank refunded in EGP after 3 years without interest; USD 250,000 non-refundable payment. USD 10,000 application fee. Selling the property or project within 5 years requires a USD 250,000 payment to keep citizenship. No residence requirement. Each grant is published as a named PM decree in the Official Gazette; no aggregate statistics are published. The 'launched' date is the decree month; applications reportedly opened in 2020.

name: Egypt 'deposit residence' (إقامة بوديعة) for foreign investors, Law 173/2018
notes: Created by Law 173/2018 (Gazette 14 Aug 2018, in force the next day): residence category for foreigners depositing at least EGP 7 million (or foreign-currency equivalent) in an Egyptian bank; after five consecutive years the Interior Minister could naturalise them, the deposit then passing to the Treasury. Implementing rules were to be set by an Interior Minister decree. Repealed by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019), which replaced it with the egy-cbi programme. No evidence found that any permit was issued; 'ended' is the month of the repealing law (Gazette publication date not verified).

name: Spain investor visa and residence authorisation (visado y autorización de residencia para inversores, Ley 14/2013, 'golden visa')
notes: Residence (not citizenship) for non-EU investors under arts. 61-67 of Ley 14/2013 (in force 29 Sep 2013). Routes: EUR 500,000 real estate per applicant; EUR 2m Spanish public debt; EUR 1m in shares of Spanish companies or in Spanish bank deposits; from 30 Jul 2015 also EUR 1m in Spanish investment/venture-capital funds; business project of general interest (no fixed amount). Visas issued by consulates (Foreign Ministry); residence authorisations granted in Spain by the Directorate-General for Migration and processed by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos (UGE-CE). Visa 1 year; initial authorisation 2 years (3 years from 23 Dec 2022); renewals 2 years, then 5 years from 30 Jul 2015. Family members got derivative permits. The law gave no shortcut to citizenship. Arts. 63-67 emptied by Ley Orgánica 1/2025 (in force 3 Apr 2025); existing permits may be renewed. Official statistics are scattered: one 2015 ministry report, parliamentary answers, and 2024 press releases whose counts do not match each other (consular visas vs all authorisations).

name: Tier 1 (Investor) visa (United Kingdom)
notes: Residence by investment under Part 6A of the Immigration Rules (paras 245E-245EF; originally 245O-245U), created by HC 607 from 30 June 2008, replacing an 'investor' category that had existed since 1 October 1994. Investors held GBP 1m (GBP 2m from 6 Nov 2014) and invested it in UK government bonds (until 29 March 2019) or share/loan capital of UK trading companies; no job or business required. First grant 3 years 4 months, extension 2 years. Settlement (indefinite leave to remain) after 5 years, or after 3 years with GBP 5m / 2 years with GBP 10m (from 6 April 2011). Citizenship by naturalisation possible 12 months after settlement and 5 years' residence (MAC 2014: 6 years at GBP 1m, 5 years at GBP 5m/10m). Closed to new applicants at 16:00 on 17 Feb 2022 by CP 632; existing investors could extend until 17 Feb 2026 and may apply to settle until 17 Feb 2028. Home Office statistics count visas per person and separate main applicants from dependants; no official figure for total money invested.

name: Greece Golden Visa (Μόνιμη άδεια διαμονής επενδυτή - permanent investor residence permit, real estate)
notes: Residence (not citizenship): five-year renewable permit, no right to work, no minimum stay; family members get derivative permits. Legal basis: art. 36A Law 3386/2005 (added by Law 4146/2013) -> art. 20(B) Law 4251/2014 -> art. 100 Law 5038/2023 (type B.5). Financial-investment permits (art. 16 Law 4251/2014 / art. 99 Law 5038/2023, type B.4) are a separate permit type. Ministry statistics count permits (one per person) and distinguish main investors vs family members and first grant vs renewal.

name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Programme (Investment Migration Agency Grenada)
notes: Legal basis: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013 and SRO 17 of 2013. First approvals 2014. Routes: NTF donation, approved real estate, significant investment (from 2024 statistics). Unit rebranded IMA in March 2024.

name: Grenada Economic Citizenship Program (1997-2001)
notes: Predecessor scheme; suspended indefinitely after 9/11 (UNGA statement Nov 2001). Details only from secondary/industry sources. Proposed as a separate program_id; merge into grd-cbi if the dataset prefers one id per jurisdiction.

name: Hungarian Guest Investor Program (vendégbefektetői vízum és tartózkodási engedély)
notes: Act XC of 2023, ss. 16 and 22: six-month guest investor visa, then a 10-year residence permit renewable for 10 more, with the right to work. Routes: EUR 250,000 in units of a qualified Hungarian real estate fund held 5 years; EUR 1,000,000 donation to a foundation-run university; EUR 500,000 residential property until removed on 30 Dec 2024. Security vetting by the Constitution Protection Office; fund managers need clearance. Law in force 1 Jan 2024, but the first fund manager qualified only in Oct 2024. No official statistics are published; press reports from OIF data show very low take-up.

name: Hungarian residency bond programme (Letelepedési Magyar Államkötvény, settlement bond)
notes: Residence permit in the 'national economic interest' under s. 28(3)-(11) of Act II of 2007 (added by Act CCXX of 2012) for holders of at least EUR 250,000 (EUR 300,000 from 2015) of five-year securities sold by private intermediaries approved by Parliament's economic committee (eight in all, mostly offshore; one per country); the intermediaries bought discounted zero-coupon euro bonds from ÁKK. Settlement (permanent residence) permit after six months, directly from July 2016 per Index. ÁKK: EUR 1.844 billion face value issued 2013-2017 in 11 series, all repaid by 2022. BMH: about 6,500 investors and 13,300 family members. Residence route only; normal naturalisation rules applied.

name: Investment-based naturalisation scheme ('passports for investment')
notes: No law of its own: the Minister for Justice used the discretion in section 16 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 1956 (as amended 1986) to waive the residence condition for investors, treating the investment as 'Irish associations'. Government approved the approach in April 1989, but the Department's review counts naturalisations from 1988 (and the 2002 Minister said it was introduced in 1988; the 2000 Minister said 1989). Applicant, spouse and children under 18 could be included. Before 1994 the Department's working rule was about IR£500,000; from October 1994 an advisory group applied a minimum net investment of IR£1 million per applicant, a residence to be kept 5 years and 60 days' presence in the 2 years after naturalisation. New applications stopped on 4 Sep 1996; the scheme was formally ended on 20 Apr 1998, but cases already accepted were processed later (naturalisations recorded up to 2004). Section 10 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 2004 removed the legal basis. Totals given to the Dáil: 143 persons by Feb 1998; 183 persons (107 investors) in the final count. The Department's 1998 review found most early cases did not meet the published conditions (e.g. good-character evidence in 17 of 66).

name: Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP)
notes: Residence by investment run by the Department of Justice (INIS, later Immigration Service Delivery) under a Government decision of 2012 and ministerial guidelines, without its own legislation. Approved investors and their spouse/partner and minor children got Stamp 4 residence (right to work and study): 2 years, renewed for 3, then 5-year renewals while the investment (held at least 3 years) stayed in place. No residence obligation beyond visiting Ireland once a year. No fast track to citizenship: naturalisation needs 5 years' physical (reckonable) residence, so investors who did not live in Ireland could not qualify. Projects were vetted by an inter-departmental Evaluation Committee; the minister decided. Most money went via the enterprise option into project vehicles (nursing homes, social housing, hotels) put together by agents for groups of mainly Chinese investors. Closed to new applications 15 Feb 2023; applications on hand and investors for already approved projects are still being processed (1,192 pending in March 2026).

name: Investor Visa for Italy (visto per investitori, art. 26-bis D.Lgs. 286/1998)
notes: Entry visa and two-year 'per investitori' residence permit, renewable for three years at a time, for non-EU nationals who invest EUR 2m in Italian government bonds, EUR 500k (EUR 1m until 18 May 2020) in an Italian company (from 18 Dec 2024 also an Italian venture-capital fund), EUR 250k (EUR 500k until 18 May 2020) in an innovative start-up, or donate EUR 1m to a public-interest project; investment must be made within 3 months of arrival and held for 2 years. Legal basis in force 1 Jan 2017 (L. 232/2016, art. 1, c. 148); implementing decree 21 Jul 2017; applications run through an online portal from 14 Dec 2017, vetted by an inter-ministerial Committee chaired by the ministry of enterprise (MISE, now MIMIT), which issues a nulla osta. No real-estate route. Applications free of charge. Holders may apply for an EU long-term permit after 5 years of holding the investment (portal); no special route to citizenship. Suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens from 14 Jul 2023 and for dual nationals with a Russian or Belarusian passport from 20 Mar 2024. Very low uptake: 13 applications to end-2019 (latest official total found).

name: Jordanian citizenship for investors (أسس منح المستثمرين الجنسية الأردنية)
notes: Not a statute: Cabinet decisions setting 'bases' for naturalising investors (Nationality Law allows Cabinet discretion). Rules changed in Dec 2019 (amounts cut), 12 Sep 2021 (decision 3657: deposit+bonds, shares, new and existing projects; 500 investors a year cap), 2022 (decision 6404: sector routes; employment route), and 2 Jul 2025 (decision 4375: amounts in JOD, deposit/bond route dropped). New-project investors first get a 3-year temporary passport (no political rights) and citizenship after 3 years of compliance. Applications go to the Ministry of Investment (earlier the Jordan Investment Commission); a special investors committee chaired by the Interior Minister (decision 5995 of 19 Aug 2019) recommends to the Cabinet; security approval is required. Launch year 2018 is reported (JIC/Jordan Times give the 'previous' amounts); the 2018 decision itself was not obtained.

name: Jordan five-year residence for property buyers (الإقامة لمدة خمس سنوات عن طريق شراء عقار)
notes: Five-year renewable residence for investors or ordinary persons buying one or more residential properties worth at least JOD 200,000 (Department of Lands and Survey valuation), held 5 years without sale or mortgage; issued by the Interior Minister on the investor committee's recommendation; spouse and children included. Since decision 4375 (2025) the purchase must be new and from a licensed developer. Residence does not lead to citizenship by itself (ordinary naturalisation rules apply). Earliest official evidence found: JIC sheet of Jan 2021; launch date not established.

name: Cambodia: naturalisation by investment or donation (Law on Nationality 1996, Arts 10-12; Law on Nationality 2018, Arts 21-22; Sub-decree No. 225 of 2025)
notes: Under the 1996 law, investors spending 1,250,000,000 riels were exempted from the 7-year residence requirement and donors of 1,000,000,000 riels to the national budget could apply; granted by Royal Decree, with an optional Khmer name. The 2018 law moved the amounts into a sub-decree (No. 112 of 30 Aug 2018, not found) and added 12 months' (investors) or 6 months' (donors) legal residence. Sub-decree No. 225 of 1 Dec 2025 sets 4,000,000,000 riel (investment in priority sectors) and 12,000,000,000 riel (donation). Naturalisations were published in the Royal Gazette until February 2024 (about 50 a month in 2020-2023, all routes); no official count by route. Several naturalised China-born businessmen were later sanctioned or prosecuted abroad.

name: St. Kitts and Nevis Citizenship by Investment Programme
notes: Oldest CBI program. Routes over time: SIDF donation (from 2006), Hurricane Relief Fund (c. 2017-2018), Sustainable Growth Fund (to July 2023), Sustainable Island State Contribution (from 27 July 2023), approved real estate, private homes, public benefit option, alternative investment options (2020-2023). CIU became a statutory body in 2024.

name: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP Saint Lucia)
notes: Act No. 14 of 2015; regulations SI 89 of 2015 (2 Oct 2015); CIU operating from Oct 2015; first applications 1 Jan 2016. Fiscal year April-March.

name: Latvia temporary residence permits for investors (Imigrācijas likums, 23. panta pirmās daļas 28.-31. punkts)
notes: Five-year renewable temporary residence permits (termiņuzturēšanās atļauja, TUA) for investors and their spouses and minor children, under art. 23(1) points 28 (company capital), 29 (real estate), 30 (subordinated liabilities with a Latvian bank) and 31 (interest-free state securities, 2015 to May 2026) of the 2002 Immigration Law; added by the law of 22.04.2010, in force 1 Jul 2010. Run by the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP). Russian and Belarusian citizens excluded from 24 Sep 2022. The state-securities route was deleted from 20 May 2026; the property and bank routes ended when the new Immigration Law took effect on 15 Sep 2026, which keeps a two-year business-investment permit and adds an (not yet operational) EUR 150,000 state fund route, so the programme continues in reduced form. Under art. 24(1) point 7 of the 2002 law, a foreigner who has lived in Latvia continuously with a temporary residence permit for at least five years may request permanent residence (other conditions, such as language, apply; not detailed here). Citizenship rules not researched.

name: Programul de dobândire a cetățeniei prin investiție (Citizenship by Investment Programme of the Republic of Moldova)
notes: Legal basis: art. 17(11)-(12) of Citizenship Law no. 1024/2000 as amended (bill registered Dec 2016) and Government Decision no. 786 of 4 Oct 2017 (regulation). Run with Henley & Partners as the government's exclusive private operator. Routes as reported in the press: a non-refundable contribution of at least EUR 100,000 to the Public Investment Fund for Sustainable Development, or an investment of EUR 250,000 in a strategic sector held 60 months. Cap of 5,000 main applicants (CJI). Launched Nov 2018; moratorium on new applications from summer 2019 (Law 107/2019), extended; Parliament abolished the scheme on 18 Jun 2020 with effect from 1 Sep 2020. 38 applications for 98 people; 20 applications (52 people) successful by mid-2021 (EC). The text of HG 786/2017 itself was not read (legis.md blocked).

name: North Macedonia: naturalisation for special economic interest (Закон за државјанството, член 11; Уредба за утврдување на критериумите за особен ... национален интерес)
notes: Art. 11 of the Law on Citizenship (since 1992; reworded 2004) allows naturalisation without residence where it is of special scientific, economic, cultural, sporting or other national interest; the Government decides. Criteria decree of 2005 (no amounts); EUR 400,000 direct investment plus 10 jobs from 20 Dec 2012; EUR 200,000 private investment fund route added 14 Dec 2019. The Ministries of Finance and Economy assess economic interest and the security agency vets. 121 economic-interest grants 2005-2022 (40 refusals); one or two a year since. The European Commission (Dec 2025) says the scheme must be abolished under the Visa Suspension Mechanism; a June 2026 draft law would remove fixed amounts but keep investment as a criterion. This row covers the economic-interest route; some observations give other Art. 11 grounds (sport, culture, science) via breakdown. 'launched' is the first criteria decree; the legal basis dates from 1992.

name: Individual Investor Programme of the Republic of Malta (IIP)
notes: Closed to new applications 31 Jul 2020. Pending applications were processed until 2024 (6 naturalisations in 2024). Cap of 1,800 main applicants; 1,555 were naturalised.

name: Maltese Citizenship by Naturalisation for Exceptional Services by Direct Investment (Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services, GCES)
notes: Found contrary to EU law by the CJEU on 29 Apr 2025 (C-181/23). Discontinued by Act XXI of 2025, whose transitional clause keeps applications filed before it under the old rules. The date new applications actually stopped (reportedly 29 Apr 2025) was not verified in a primary source.

name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
notes: Successor to the Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP). Run by Residency Malta Agency. No official application or approval statistics were found.

name: Posebni program ulaganja od posebnog značaja za privredni i ekonomski interes Crne Gore (Special Investment Programme of Special Importance for the Economic Interest of Montenegro; "economic citizenship")
notes: Created by Government decision of 22 Nov 2018 (Službeni list CG 79/2018); applications from 1 Jan 2019. Applicant pays EUR 100,000 into an escrow account for less developed municipalities and invests at least EUR 450,000 (Podgorica or coast) or EUR 250,000 (north/centre) in a government-listed development project (in practice condo-hotel units), plus fees of EUR 15,000 per applicant and EUR 10,000 per family member. From 31 Dec 2021 an extra EUR 100,000 to the Innovation Fund. Cap of 2,000 decisions. Applications only through licensed intermediary agents (Henley & Partners, Arton, Apex), with due-diligence agents. Originally to end 31 Dec 2021; extended on 30 Dec 2021 to 31 Dec 2022, then expired; pending applications still decided in 2026 (5 left on 1 Sep 2026). 1,113 applications filed nationally, 869 approved, 239 refused; the EC counts 556 main applicants with 1,281 family members. Over 70% of passports to 2022 went to Russian citizens (EC).

name: Nauru Citizen Investor scheme (Nauruan Community Act 1956-1997, s. 5(6)-(9))
notes: Created by the Nauruan Community Ordinance Amendment Act 1997 (No. 11 of 1997): citizenship for a person who made an investment "of such form and in such amount as determined by Cabinet", vetted by a Nauru Citizen Investment Board. Dates of operation (1998 to 2003), the about 1,000 sales and the end after concerns about passports used by suspected terrorists come from an academic report citing secondary work, not from official records.

name: Nauru (Naoero) Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program (NECRCP / ECRCP)
notes: Set up by the Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15 of 2024, certified 20 Aug 2024); prices in Regulations SL 28 of 2024 (gazetted 30 Oct 2024). Unveiled at COP29 on 13 Nov 2024 and launched by the President in Singapore on 28 Nov 2024; the IMF gives 2025 as inception year. One route: a non-refundable contribution to the Treasury Fund, applications only through licensed agents, run by a Program Office based in Auckland and operated by a private firm. Prices were restructured on 29 Jan 2026 (USD 115,000 single applicant) and a temporary USD 90,000 discount applies to 31 Dec 2026. No official statistics on applications or grants are published; the IMF reports FY2025 revenue of AU$0.24 million and the authorities cite low take-up.

name: Panama Friendly Nations residence (Residente Permanente en calidad de nacionales de países específicos que mantienen relaciones amistosas, profesionales, económicas y de inversión; 'Países Amigos')
notes: Residence for nationals of a closed list of countries (24 in 2012, about 50 by 2021). First created by DE 343 of 16 May 2012 (not seen; known from its repeal), replaced by DE 416 of 13 June 2012 (Gaceta 27058-A). Until 2021 it needed only an economic or professional activity and a modest bank balance, not an investment. From 7 Aug 2021 (DE 197 and DE 226 of 2021) applicants get a two-year provisional permit and must show either a job with a work permit, real estate worth at least B/.200,000, or a B/.200,000 three-year fixed deposit; permanent residence follows after two years. Not an investment programme in the strict sense: the SNM statistics count all Friendly Nations permits, whatever the route. Naturalisation rules are the general constitutional ones (not checked in this pass).

name: Panama residence as investor in a large business (Inversionista de Macro-empresa)
notes: Residence for foreigners who are sole holders of shares worth at least B/.160,000 in a company with a commercial licence (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 185-186). SNM approvals fell to 10-15 a year by 2020-2021; the category no longer appears separately in the 2022-2026 tables. Current status not checked.

name: Panama Qualified Investor Program (Residente Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado)
notes: Direct permanent residence (no provisional stage) for a qualifying investment from foreign funds, held for five years. Two steps: MICI (Dirección Nacional de Promoción de la Inversión) issues an investment certificate, then the SNM grants the permit (30 working days by decree). Created by Decreto Ejecutivo 722 of 15 Oct 2020 (Gaceta 29136, 16 Oct 2020); amended by DE 109 of 2022 and DE 193 of 2024; replaced ('subrogado') by DE 17 of 8 Sept 2026 (Gaceta 30613, 16 Sept 2026). Routes: real estate (incl. presale contracts), securities via the Panama stock exchange, fixed-term bank deposit. Citizenship: DE 17 art. 14 says holders and dependants may apply for naturalisation after five consecutive years of residence, under the Constitution. Applications can be filed from abroad through a lawyer.

name: Panama permanent residence for own economic solvency (Residente Permanente por Solvencia Económica Propia)
notes: Older investor residence under the 2008 migration regulation (DE 320 of 8 Aug 2008, arts. 191-195): B/.300,000 of foreign funds in real estate, a three-year fixed deposit, or a mix of both. SNM statistics show it as a provisional permit followed by a permanent one. A similar 'Solvencia Propia' status existed before 2008 under Decreto Ley 16 of 1960 (the SNM series from 2010 includes it). DE 722 of 2020 and DE 17 of 2026 let pending or current Solvencia holders switch to the Qualified Investor route. Amendments after 2008 were not checked.

name: Portugal Golden Visa (Autorização de Residência para Atividade de Investimento, ARI)
notes: Residence permit for investment under art. 90-A of the Foreigners Act (Law 23/2007), created by Law 29/2012. Temporary permit (now two years, renewable for two-year periods) without a residence visa; minimum stay 7 days in the first year and 14 days in each later two-year period; family reunification. Routes over time: capital transfer (EUR 1m, then EUR 1.5m), job creation (30, then 10 jobs), real estate (EUR 500k), rehabilitation property (EUR 350k), research (EUR 350k, then 500k), culture (EUR 250k), funds (EUR 500k/350k/500k) and company capital with jobs (EUR 350k, then 500k). Residential property limited to the interior and islands from 2022; real estate and capital transfer closed to new applications by Law 56/2023 (Mais Habitação) from 7 Oct 2023. Run by SEF until 28 Oct 2023, then AIMA. Path to citizenship: naturalisation after 6 years of legal residence (2012-2018), 5 years (from 6 Jul 2018; from 1 Apr 2024 counted from the permit application), and from 19 May 2026 10 years (7 for CPLP/EU nationals), with pending applications kept under the old law. 12,718 investor permits and 20,424 family permits were granted under SEF (Oct 2012-Sep 2023), with EUR 7.32bn of reported investment.

name: Financial Investor Scheme (FIS)
notes: Separate investor permanent-residence scheme. 1,080 investors granted PR from 2004 to 2012; 194 applications rejected. Ceased 15 Apr 2012. Investment terms not found in official sources read (an MP said in 2012 that MAS had withdrawn it). Launch year taken from the period in the parliamentary answer ('From 2004 to 2012'), not confirmed.

name: Global Investor Programme (GIP)
notes: Permanent residence (not citizenship) for business owners and investors, run by Contact Singapore, a division of the Economic Development Board (EDB); approvals issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority. No law establishing the scheme was found; it is run administratively. MTI dates it to 2004, though a 2005 ministerial statement refers to GIP rules changed in 1996. Applicants must first meet business track-record tests (e.g. company turnover of S$200m now) or, for family-office principals, S$200m in net investible assets; then invest under Option A (business, S$10m since 15 Mar 2023), B (GIP-select fund, S$25m) or C (single family office, AUM S$200m with S$50m deployed in Singapore, since Feb 2025 in listed equities). PR comes with a 5-year re-entry permit renewed only if business, jobs and residence conditions are met. Citizenship is not part of the scheme: GIP PRs may apply for it through the normal process (67 of 1,826 had by June 2017). Separate from the MAS 13O/13U family-office tax incentives, which give no residence rights.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment or Donation Programme (Programa de Cidadania por Investimento ou Doação, PCID)
notes: Legal basis: Nationality Law No. 7/2022 of 10 Mar 2022 (art. 10(2), art. 26) and Decree-Law No. 07/2025 (approved 10 May 2025, published and in force 1 Aug 2025), which creates the programme, the Citizenship by Investment and Donation Unit (UCID, under the Justice Minister) and the National Transformation Fund (FNT). One route: non-refundable contribution to the FNT after approval in principle (USD 90,000 single applicant). The Decree-Law requires quarterly reports to the Justice Minister, Public Prosecutor and National Assembly and an annual independent audit of the FNT; none were found published. The programme site claims more than 220 applications by 2 Mar 2026. A formal national launch conference was held in Oct 2025.

name: Tonga passport and citizenship sales (Tongan Protected Person passports and naturalisation), proceeds held in the Tonga Trust Fund
notes: Proposed to the King by Hong Kong businessman George Chen. First 'Tongan Protected Person' passports (travel document, no right to live in Tonga), later full Tongan nationality. Buyers were mostly Hong Kong Chinese; Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos were among them. Press accounts give 1983-1991, over 5,000 sold and about $30 million raised (currency not stated); the US State Department still said Tonga sold economic citizenship in 2000. The money was held in the Tonga Trust Fund at Bank of America, San Francisco; from 1999 it was managed on the advice of the King's 'court jester' Jesse Bogdonoff and largely lost in Millennium Asset Management (viatical insurance). Tonga sued in San Francisco in June 2002 and settled in February 2004. No official Tongan document found.

name: Turkish citizenship by investment (Türk Vatandaşlığı Kanununun Uygulanmasına İlişkin Yönetmelik, Art. 20(2))
notes: Exceptional naturalisation under Law 5901 Art. 12(1)(b) by presidential decision (Council of Ministers until Sept 2018). Routes: real estate, fixed capital, jobs, bank deposit, government bonds, investment funds, private pension (from 2022). Certifying bodies: TKGM/Ministry of Environment (real estate), Ministry of Industry, Ministry of Labour, BDDK, Treasury, SPK, SEDDK. Security vetting by police and MİT; decision prepared by the DG of Population and Citizenship Affairs.

name: EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program (employment-based fifth preference, INA 203(b)(5)), including the Regional Center Program
notes: Created by sec. 121 of the Immigration Act of 1990 (signed 29 Nov 1990; preference system in force from 1 Oct 1991, FY1992). Investors who invest the minimum in a new commercial enterprise creating 10 full-time jobs get two-year conditional permanent residence (green card) for themselves, spouse and children under 21, then file Form I-829 to remove conditions. Naturalisation is possible after five years of permanent residence (8 U.S.C. 1427). Regional Center Program added as a pilot in 1992 (sec. 610, Pub. L. 102-395), repeatedly extended, lapsed 1 July 2021-14 March 2022, reauthorised by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (Pub. L. 117-103, div. BB) in force from 14 May 2022 through 30 Sep 2027; regional-center petitions filed by 30 Sep 2026 are protected if the program lapses. Annual quota about 7.1% of employment-based visas (10,000 in the 1990 Act), with 20% rural, 10% high-unemployment and 2% infrastructure set-asides since 2022. First automatic inflation adjustment of the minimum investment due for petitions filed from 1 Jan 2027 (amount not yet published as of 2 Oct 2026). Run by USCIS (Immigrant Investor Program Office); visas allocated by the State Department.

name: Gold Card programme ('Trump Gold Card'), Executive Order 14351
notes: Established by Executive Order 14351 (19 Sep 2025), not by statute: an unrestricted gift to the Department of Commerce (USD 1 million for an individual, USD 2 million from a corporation for an employee) is treated as evidence for existing EB-1 (extraordinary ability) or EB-2 (exceptional ability / national-interest waiver) immigrant classifications, with expedited processing. Applicants register and pay on trumpcard.gov (Department of Commerce), then file Form I-140G online with USCIS (fee USD 15,000 per person); the gift is paid after vetting. Leads to ordinary permanent residence (not conditional), so naturalisation after five years under 8 U.S.C. 1427. The order asks agencies to consider extending it to EB-5. No official figures on applications, approvals or money received were found. The 'Trump Platinum Card' (USD 5 million) is only announced on trumpcard.gov ('Coming Soon'); no legal act creating it was found. Statutory basis and visa-number limits remain those of EB-1/EB-2.

name: St Vincent and the Grenadines economic citizenship programme (2000-2001)
notes: Legislative framework created around 2000; the government projected about US$4.5 million in 2000 from passport sales. Revoked in April 2001; the US State Department says no passports had been issued. Only source found: US INCSR.

name: 1990s passport-sale schemes
notes: The IMF (2015) describes attempts in the 1990s to sell passports, about 300 passports sold in 1996-1997, and reports of illegal issuance that led some countries, such as Canada, to drop visa waivers. Names, legal basis and dates not found in official sources.

name: Vanuatu investor citizenship schemes (all schemes; the IMF's "Economic Citizenship Program", ECP)
notes: Umbrella id for figures that cover several schemes at once. Government accounts book VDSP and VCP receipts together as "Honorary Citizenship Program Fees" and, from 2024, report them together with the CIIP. Schemes over time: 1990s passport sales; CIIP (2014-); VERP honorary citizenship (2015-March 2017); VDSP and VCP (2017-); REO (2021-). Run by the Citizenship Office and Commission; due diligence by the Financial Intelligence Unit. Citizenship is granted without residence; Part 3A of the Citizenship Act allows dual citizenship.

name: Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP)
notes: Citizenship for investors (Form D), legal basis s.13B-13C of the Citizenship Act inserted by Act No. 39 of 2013 (in force 21 Jan 2014), linked to a residence permit under the Immigration Visa Regulation No. 180 of 2011. IMF (2015): USD 260,000 investment returnable after 7 years (25% NBV deposit, 25% government bonds, 50% real investment) plus a $40,000 fee. The Citizenship Office now lists a "Citizenship Fee" of USD 260,000 for applicant, spouse and one child. Practically dormant in 2020 (VT 10,000 receipts), reactivated as a cheaper alternative in 2024, suspended March 2025 and resumed June 2025 (IMF).

name: Vanuatu Development Support Program (DSP / VDSP)
notes: Main scheme since 2017; first run as "Honorary Citizenship DSP" (fees reduced by Order No. 94 of 2018), put on a statutory footing by s.13E (Act No. 34 of 2018, in force 7 Jan 2019) and regulated by Order No. 33 of 2019 (24 Apr 2019): government fee USD 80,000 (single) to 130,000 (couple and two children), minimum selling price via licensed Vanuatu-citizen agents USD 130,000 to 180,000, FIU due diligence (USD 2,000, USD 5,000 from 27 Mar 2020). Decision within 3 months; no residence required.

name: Hong Kong Permanent Residency (HKPR) Visa Program
notes: Residence (not citizenship) for mainland Chinese investors seeking Hong Kong permanent residency via Hong Kong's Capital Investment Entrant Scheme: investment of at least 300,000 vatu in a Vanuatu company through a Hong Kong agent, 10-year visa. About 1,500 investors; suspended after Hong Kong suspended its scheme in January 2015 (IMF). No path to citizenship stated.

name: Real Estate Option Program (REO)
notes: Citizenship for buying property in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project plus prescribed fees; s.13F of the Citizenship Act and Regulation Order No. 93 of 2021; sole master agent Naika Holdings Ltd. An earlier REO route (s.13CA, Act No. 18 of 2014, in force 8 Jul 2014) was repealed by Act No. 40 of 2014 (23 Jan 2015). The Treasury said in 2021-22 its revenue potential was low or unproven. Prices not found.

name: Vanuatu Contribution Program (VCP)
notes: Legal basis s.13D of the Citizenship Act and the Citizenship (Contribution Program) Regulations Order No. 220 of 2016 (not found online); amended by Order No. 34 of 2019 and Order No. 38 of 2020. Same government minimum contribution and minimum selling price as the DSP (Citizenship Office directive, April 2020). Launch date taken from the Treasury statement that VDSP and VCP replaced VERP by March 2017. Industry sources say it was reserved for Chinese applicants; not confirmed officially.

name: Vanuatu Economic Rehabilitation Program (VERP), honorary citizenship after Cyclone Pam
notes: Honorary citizenship sold to raise revenue after Cyclone Pam (March 2015), using the honorary citizenship power in s.20 of the Citizenship Act. ABC reported a launch in Hong Kong in April 2015 (price $162,000, quota 100); the IMF dates the launch to late 2015. Phased out by March 2017 and replaced by the VDSP and VCP (Treasury).
